Zillow Group (Z) — key metrics

Z-zbar-2026-09-28-v3 · USD · series 2026-09-29T06:40:00Z · built 2026-09-29 02:44 UTC

The short version

Own Z for five to ten years as a housing marketplace with data and network effects — not a banner shop waiting for ChatGPT to erase the front door. What would change that view first is a sustained multi-quarter drop in monthly audience or issuer-quoted audience share. A second warning would be Google or ChatGPT taking a meaningful and rising slice of housing search (roughly five percent or more) — that share series is still blank in the public record we use. This page is the income, margins, shares, mix, traffic, and trailing-multiple scoreboard — full history where each print exists, including operating income beside adjusted EBITDA, diluted share count, EPS, and operating income per share. Preferred attachment, For Sale take intensity, and relative revenue-per-connection uplift live on the companion dig: https://latentcapitalventures.github.io/research-site/Z-unit-econ-2026-09-28/

Zillow Desk · Latent capital · as of 2026-09-28 (EDT)

How it makes money

Zillow Group runs consumer brands — Zillow, Trulia, StreetEasy, HotPads — that pull demand for homes and apartments. Revenue shows up in three engines:

  1. Residential — Premier Agent and Preferred-style connection advertising, plus related for-sale marketplace products.
  2. Mortgages — including Zillow Home Loans purchase origination.
  3. Rentals — multifamily and rental marketplace revenue.

From fourth-quarter 2024 on, the company prints a For Sale subtotal (Residential plus Mortgages) in the segment table we treat as fact. Rentals stands alone. Earlier modern quarters on the For Sale chart are Residential plus Mortgages, marked derived. Homes-era labels are not For Sale.

Resid, Mort, and Rentals as themselves — not a pre-2023 relabel.

For Sale runs from early 2023, marked derived through third-quarter 2024 and printed from fourth-quarter 2024. Rentals is the second locomotive on the same front door.

In second-quarter 2026 the company printed $772M total revenue, $549M For Sale, $209M Rentals, operating income −$10M (margin −1.3%), adjusted EBITDA $176M (margin 22.8%), GAAP loss −$4M / diluted EPS −$0.02, and diluted weighted-average shares 227.9M. Cash was $572M. Survival is not the open question. Mix quality and take-rate are — and those sit on the unit-econ dig.

Four series side by side from the mid-2010s where each print exists. Blank cells stay blank. The 2021 scale spike is the Homes / iBuying company total — not marketplace-only — so the era is labeled on the chart.

Same history, in percent. GAAP operating margin is still near flat to negative while adjusted EBITDA margin holds in the low-to-mid 20s on recent marketplace quarters.

Share count through the Class C era and the recent buyback path. Early-2015 prints are the smaller pre-Class-C base, labeled on the chart. A handful of fourth quarters stay blank.

EPS is the printed figure when the filing has one. Otherwise it is net income over diluted shares, marked derived. Operating income per share uses that same share base and is marked derived.

Audience — soft, not collapsing

Q2’26 visits 2,529M / AMUU 239 versus Q2’25 2,590M / 243 — soft year-over-year, not a sustained collapse. Fourth-quarter prints are on the series: Q4’23 2,200 / 194, Q4’24 2,100 / 204, Q4’25 2,100 / 221.

Using Comscore figures the company itself quotes, Zillow Group held about 70% of the real-estate audience in both first- and second-quarter 2026. That is the sharper front-door print than raw AMUU alone.
